May is Military Appreciation Month.

No speech captures it. No ceremony is enough. The men and women who put on the uniform and step into harm's way so the rest of us don't have to deserve more than a month.

In SC-01, we are surrounded by their service. Joint Base Charleston. Parris Island. Beaufort MCAS. Thousands of veterans across every county in our district.

May God bless each and every one of our service members, past, present, and future. Thank you for your service.

15 years ago today, SEAL Team Six shot and killed Osama Bin Laden. The monster responsible for the 9/11 attacks, killing 2,977 people. 

One of the greatest military accomplishments in our nation's history. A day we were united as a country and as patriots. May the world never forget what American strength looks like, the same way we will never forget September 11th, 2001. 

Chills.

The federal government has been writing regulations for decades without ever calculating what they cost the American household.

Our military is the greatest fighting force the world has ever seen. Not because of politics. Not because of ideology. Because of the extraordinary Americans with the courage to defend our freedom at any cost. 

They deserve a government willing to match their courage, both while serving and when they return home.
The Left was more willing to fund insect research in Africa just a few months ago than they are to fund the men and women who protect our country's border.

We can't expect to be healthy while eating food coated in poison. 

Stripping pesticide liability protections from the Farm Bill is a huge step in the right direction toward Making America Healthy Again.

We stood with MAHA movement in support of the Luna Amendment to strip pesticide protections from the Farm Bill.

No corporation should be shielded from accountability and no state and local voices should be silenced, when their chemicals are poisoning people and linked to cancer. This is a huge win for states' rights, public health, and the American people.

This is what Making America Healthy Again looks like.

If SNAP recipients want to buy sugary drinks, they can do it on their own dime, not on the backs of a taxpayer-funded nutrition program.
